questions.heading: Variables, Rows and the Objective Come From the Solver, in Two Styles
questions.stem: A script calls CreateSolver("GLOP"), makes n = IntVar(0, 10, "n"), adds the row 4n <= 18 and maximizes n. Solve() returns 0. What does n.solution_value() give?

options.text: 4.0, because the solver rounds the LP answer down to a whole number
options.says: GLOP solves the LP relaxation and returns its answer without rounding.

options.text: 4.5, because an LP back end ignores that the variable was declared integer
options.says: Right: GLOP is an LP solver; it returned y = 2.5 for IntVar variables in the lesson's run.

options.text: None, because CreateSolver refuses integer variables for an LP back end
options.says: CreateSolver returned a solver, and IntVar was accepted; the lesson's third run shows status 0.

options.text: 5.0, because the solver rounds the LP answer up to a whole number
options.says: No rounding happens, and rounding up would break the row 4n <= 18.

questions.heading: Variables, Rows and the Objective Come From the Solver, in Two Styles
questions.stem: A legacy script builds row = solver.RowConstraint(3, 12, "load"), then row.SetCoefficient(a, 1) and row.SetCoefficient(b, 2). Which rule does the solver hold?

options.text: a + 2b <= 12 alone, since the 3 is where the solver starts its search
options.says: The first argument is the row's lower bound, not a starting point.

options.text: a + 2b = 12 - 3, since the two numbers give the row's net right side
options.says: The two numbers are a lower and an upper bound, not terms of one side.

options.text: a + 2b >= 3 alone, since a second number on a row is ignored
options.says: Both bounds are kept; the LP export writes them as two lines, _lhs and _rhs.

options.text: 3 <= a + 2b <= 12, since a row has a lower and an upper bound
options.says: Right: RowConstraint(lb, ub) is a ranged row, lb <= sum <= ub.

questions.heading: Solve Returns an Integer Status, and Values Exist Only When It Says So
questions.stem: A nightly job calls Solve(), which returns 2, and then prints every variable's solution_value() into a report. What does the report show?

options.text: Every variable at 0.0, since pywraplp answers value queries even with no solution
options.says: Right: status 2 is INFEASIBLE, and solution_value() still answered 0.0 in the lesson's run.

options.text: Nothing at all, since pywraplp raises an error when a value has no solution
options.says: pywraplp raised nothing; MathOpt is the API that raises in this case.

options.text: The last plan found, since pywraplp keeps the best plan seen before stopping
options.says: Status 2 is INFEASIBLE: there is no plan to keep.

options.text: The LP relaxation's values, since pywraplp falls back to them with no solution
options.says: No fallback happens; the values read 0.0.
